title: Ultrafast Mode: A Frontier Model at 750 Tokens/Second
hook: OpenAI is previewing a service tier that runs GPT-5.6 Sol up to 14x faster on Cerebras hardware — same model, different silicon, up to 750 output tokens per second.
key_points: Ultrafast is a new OpenAI API service tier, not a new model — it serves GPT-5.6 Sol at up to 14x the standard speed.
Throughput is quoted at up to 750 output tokens per second.
The tier is powered by Cerebras, meaning OpenAI is serving a frontier model on non-NVIDIA accelerators.
Speed at this level changes what's buildable: interactive agent loops and long reasoning traces stop feeling like batch jobs.
content_html: OpenAI is previewing Ultrafast, an API service tier that runs GPT-5.6 Sol at up to 14x its usual speed — quoted at up to 750 output tokens per second. The model itself is unchanged; what changes is the hardware underneath, which OpenAI says is powered by Cerebras.
extra_html:
Two things make this worth noticing beyond the number. First, latency at this scale is qualitative, not incremental: a reasoning trace or a multi-step agent loop that took a minute of visible waiting becomes something a user can sit through, which shifts what product shapes are viable. Second, a frontier OpenAI model served on Cerebras wafer-scale hardware is a real signal about where inference is heading — the model and the accelerator are increasingly separable, and speed is becoming a purchasable axis alongside capability and price.

It's a preview, so availability, rate limits, and pricing details are best read from OpenAI's post directly.
